title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 17-19). Grothendieck sets up a dictionary for the 'paradigm' of an algebraic curve over a field. In that dictionary G plays the role of Gal(kbar/k), pi the geometric fundamental group, and E the arithmetic fundamental group.

One side of the dictionary is datum A = (E, G, pi, Z). Here 1 -> pi -> E -> G -> 1 is an extension and Z is a non-empty E-set on which pi acts freely. Z is to be thought of as a Galois-stable set of 'base points' or points of the universal cover.

The other side is datum B = (Pi, Pi~, p, G, ~):
- Pi is a connected groupoid.
- p: Pi~ -> Pi is a universal covering. Pi~ is a discrete category, i.e. a discrete fibration over Pi with simply connected (trivial-isotropy) total space.
- G acts on Pi.
- '~' is the extra structure saying that the action is liftable to Pi~.

The map alpha (previous page) builds B from A:
- Ob Pi = Z/pi.
- Isom(j, j') = Isom_pi(Z_j, Z_j'), the pi-equivariant bijections between orbits; each orbit is a pi-torsor.
- Pi~ is the discrete category on Z, equal to Pi/F for the functor F(j) = Z_j.
- E acts on Pi~ and induces an action of G = E/pi on Pi.

This page defines the inverse map beta:
- E = {(g, gbar) : g in G, gbar in Aut(Pi~) compatible with g}.
- pi = Aut(Pi~/Pi), the deck group.
- The map E -> G is (g, gbar) -> g, giving 1 -> pi -> E -> G -> 1.
- Z = Ob Pi~ with its evident E-action.

The point is that an extension of G by pi, together with a set of 'universal-cover base points', is equivalent to a G-action on the fundamental groupoid based at Z/pi, lifted to the universal cover. He notes that profinite variants are needed and leaves them as 'Variantes profinies ...'.

Section (8) adds cusp/inertia data on top of A, i.e. a quadruple (chi, C, T, Phi):
- C is an E-set (the cusps 'upstairs', i.e. in the universal cover).
- T is a group, presumably Zhat.
- chi: G -> Aut(T), presumably Zhat*, the cyclotomic character.
- Phi: C -> Hom_gr(T, pi) is E-equivariant. E acts on Hom(T, pi) through chi on T and by inner automorphisms on pi.

Each point c in C thus gives an inertia homomorphism Zhat(1) -> pi, and these are permuted by E with the cyclotomic twist. On the next page he sets J = C/pi (the punctures, a G-set). He forms the groupoid <T, J>: objects J, Aut(J) = T, no maps between distinct objects. He then aims to build a G-equivariant groupoid morphism <T, J> -> Pi^ (the groupoid of universal coverings, i.e. a profinite completion).

In modern terms this encodes a profinite surface group with its peripheral (cuspidal inertia) structure and outer Galois action in groupoid language. It is the datum of an 'arithmetic curve of type (g, nu)' with tangential/cuspidal base points.
errors: Surjectivity of E -> G is asserted without comment. It holds because Pi~ is the universal cover of a connected groupoid, so every automorphism of Pi lifts. This presumably is what the datum '~' guarantees; otherwise the sequence is only left exact.
Depending on conventions, pi = Aut(Pi~/Pi) recovers pi or pi^op (Aut_pi of a torsor is the opposite group). This is harmless but unaddressed.
In the profinite case, discrete Aut groups must be replaced by profinite ones with continuous actions. Grothendieck only flags this as 'Variantes profinies ...'.
Notation drifts: E on this page becomes Sigma on the next page. In (8) he writes 'triple' but lists four items (chi was added later).

ideas.what: Equivalence between group extensions 1->pi->E->G->1 with a free pi-set Z, and G-actions on a connected groupoid lifted to its universal (discrete) covering
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid/covering description of extensions; Galois action on fundamental groupoid with many base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Brown, Higgins on groupoids and coverings); fundamental groupoid with many base points in anabelian context: Grothendieck, Deligne (1989), Ihara
ideas.where_published: Fundamental groupoid with Galois-stable set of base points is advocated in Esquisse d'un programme and the 1983 letter to Faltings; this precise dictionary is not written out there

ideas.what: Cusp datum: E-set C with E-equivariant Phi: C -> Hom(T, pi), T ~ Zhat with G acting via a character to Zhat*
ideas.modern_name: Cuspidal inertia subgroups / peripheral structure with cyclotomic twist Zhat(1); cuspidal decomposition groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in anabelian geometry (Grothendieck's program; Nakamura, Mochizuki, Ihara, 1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller groupoids and fundamental groups of type (g,nu) with loops around punctures; no explicit formulation like this

ideas.what: Groupoid <T,J> (each puncture an object with automorphism group T) mapped G-equivariantly into the groupoid of universal coverings Pi^
ideas.modern_name: Peripheral system as a morphism of groupoids; inertia at cusps as tangential-base-point data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in work on tangential base points (Deligne, Ihara, Nakamura)

deep.surprise_reason: The page carefully but routinely writes the inverse of a classical correspondence between extensions and lifted groupoid actions. It then begins encoding cuspidal inertia with cyclotomic twist, now standard in anabelian geometry. The groupoid packaging is characteristic of Grothendieck, but nothing here is absent from the later literature in substance.
transcription_corrections: 'g in G' is written beneath the line, inserted between 'E = groupe des couples (g, gbar), avec' and 'gbar in Aut(Pi~) comp. ...'. Before 'avec g' the image reads something like 'comp. dist.' (abbreviated), not clearly 'compatible'.
Z is written in fraktur-like script; E (Sigma-like) is later written as Sigma on the next page.
In (8), 'triple (C, T, Phi)' has chi inserted above the line afterwards.
The line 'chi: G -> Aut(T), (≃ Zhat* si T≃Zhat ?)' is a parenthetical gloss squeezed under 'Sigma-ens, T un groupe (≃ Zhat ?)'.
'Z = Ob Pi~, avec opération évidente de E sur Z' is a plausible reading of the abbreviated script.
